page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose server powered by an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 120 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 400 GB SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The virtualization is managed via KVM.

Performance benchmarks reflect the older CPU architecture. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. However, the 32 dedicated physical cores compensate in parallelized tasks, yielding average multi-core results in stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations sits in the middle tier, as do database operations and Redis SET throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the b2-120 is its low single-threaded efficiency compared to newer CPU generations, making it less suitable for single-core intensive tasks or real-time LLM text generation. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a dense allocation of 32 dedicated physical cores and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without hyperthreading overhead. This makes it a viable option for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose database operations that benefit from parallel execution rather than high single-core clock speeds.
